title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap + kernel scheduler + KV-cache optimizations
author: Lina Park
description: Motivation: Prefill vs decode pipeline inefficiencies surface when long context prefill work blocks low-latency decode streams and prevents continuous batching from amortizing kernel overhead. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes (chunked prefill, speculative prefill, stage overlap, KV-cache prefetch/eviction heuristics, and kernel scheduling hints) to improve tail latency and throughput for mixed prefill/decode workloads. Summary of changes: chunked prefill: break large prefill requests into configurable sub-chunks so prefill work can be interleaved with decode; speculative prefill: start background prefill for likely next token prefix (heuristic-based) to reduce critical-path KV misses; stage overlap: pipeline prefill/decode stages to allow decode kernels to run while remaining prefill chunks complete; kernel scheduler: add short-task prioritization and locality hints to reduce scheduling starvation for low-latency decodes; KV-cache: introduce prefetch-on-prefill and adaptive eviction for hot KV entries to reduce cache thrash; continuous batching: reduce batching window spikes by adding dynamic windowing based on observed latency SLOs. Benchmarks (internal dev cluster, A100-40GB, mixed workloads): median token throughput +22% on long-context chat workloads; p99 latency reduced 14%-32% depending on decode/prefill ratio (best improvements when prefill constitutes >30% of request tokens); end-to-end cost per token decreased ~10% due to better batching utilization. Backwards compatibility & flags: all behavior gated behind runtime feature flag prefill_decode_pipeline_v2 (disabled by default for private installs until QA). Exposed tuning flags: prefill_chunk_size, speculative_prefill_enabled, scheduler_short_task_threshold, kv_prefetch_ratio. Testing: added unit + integration tests for chunking logic, KV prefetch correctness, and scheduler heuristics; added new bench harness scenarios to perf-canary for automated comparison. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Canary fleet → Dedicated reserved hosts → full-hosted rollout with traffic shaping; monitoring dashboards added to Redwood Console: prefill-chunk-latency, speculative-prefill-hitrate, kv-prefetch-efficacy. Breaking changes: none to public API. Files changed (high level): serving/prefill_manager.rs, serving/pipeline/scheduler.rs, serving/kv_cache.rs, serving/batching/continuous.rs, bench/perf_canary/prefill_decode_scenarios.py, tests/prefill_chunking_test.rs, docs/runbooks/prefill-decode-ops.md. Implementation notes: prefer lock-free queue for chunk handoff to avoid contention; scheduler uses backpressure token to prevent decode starvation; speculative prefill uses a small beam (default 2) and is bounded by a CPU+mem budget to avoid cost regressions. Known limitations: degenerate pathological token distributions can still cause some KV churn; we added telemetry to detect and auto-disable speculative prefill for tenants that regress. Related work: builds on prior prefill/decode overlap PRs (see pr-71234, pr-77210, pr-79235) and the kernel-scheduler refactor in pr-48612. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1289) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf benchmarks added [x] docs/runbook updated [x] staged rollout plan added.
